bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: NLEM price cuts remain structural risk for GenMeds (though current portfolio is NLEM-resilient); supply chain dependency on CMOs (past fire incident caused INR25-30cr revenue loss); oncology adoption speed dependent on HCP education and reimbursement; currency and API price volatility
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: highly confident, transformational, and disciplined; management emphasizes sustainability over margin expansion, highlights portfolio shift from volume to value, and frames oncology/vaccines as future growth engines; tone is strategic, data-driven, and investor-aligned
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Shingrix’s CVMD linkage is a unique commercial differentiator — not just a vaccine but a preventive cardiology tool; oncology field force is tiny (25 KAS) but highly targeted (1,000 oncologists), enabling high ROI despite low headcount; digital touchpoints (4M/quarter) now complement and extend field force, reducing need for large-scale MR expansion
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The deck states a 'sustained focus to strengthen and optimize the balance sheet'.
- PAT for the quarter was helped by a one-off dividend from Biddle Sawyer Limited, described as a 100% subsidiary.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: GenMeds: +9% market growth, brands Augmentin/Ceftum/T-Bact grew double digits; Vaccines: +11% YoY, led by Boostrix/Varilrix/Havrix; Shingrix: ~INR75cr annual run rate (CY25), 80% growth YoY, now tied to CVMD strategy; Specialty: Zejula/Jemperli launched in Q3, first full quarter with 250+ patients on therapy; Jemperli gained first-line endometrial cancer approval in Dec 2025, expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; pipeline includes Belantamab (multiple myeloma), Bepirovirsen (chronic Hep B functional cure), RSV vaccine, Efimosfermin (liver disease)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- The deck says the GSK portfolio (all Gen Med and Vaccine brands except the GoA portfolio and discontinued brands) 'has maintained its leadership with 23% share in rep market', with GSK's rep market growing 10% versus GSK portfolio growth of 11% (Price 2.4%, Vol 4.4%, NI 1.8%).
- Segment leadership is claimed on both sides of the portfolio: Gen Med portfolio 'maintained its leadership with 22% share in rep market' (rep market 9% vs GSK 11%) and the Vaccines portfolio 'maintained its leadership with 27% share in rep market' — though for Vx the deck shows the rep market at 20% against the GSK Vx portfolio at 14%.
- Established Vaccines is described as continuing to lead the overall Vx market with 26.1% Value market share (MAT), at Unit EI 95 and Val EI 93; the deck states Paediatric Vaccines 'continued leadership in the self pay private pediatric market'.
- Individual brands are shown holding large shares of their own markets in Q1 FY27: T-Bact 57.5% (+2.6%), Calpol 31.2% (+1.6%), Ceftum 32.7% (+0.2%) and Augmentin 22% (+1.0%), with Key Promoted Brands at 23.4% (0%).
- GSK's growth is said to have outgrown the market in metro class and specialties, while the deck notes GPs 'continue to dominate with 40% Rxns volume and growth faster than Specialty and Super specialty Rxns'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership] Bhushan Akshikar has been MD of GSK India since Q3 2022 (15+ years at GSK across India, Middle East, Russia CIS and Africa; prior 15 years at Johnson & Johnson); Ronojit Biswas has been CFO since April 2026, previously Senior Finance Director – Global Product Strategy for General Medicines and CFO for GSK's Brazil and Vietnam businesses.
- [Market context] The deck reports IPM grew 13.5% in Q1 FY27 and separately shows IPM growth of 13.6% for Apr-May'26 attributed largely to price (Volume 8.7%, NI 1.9%, Price 3.0% are the components shown); chronic (40% of industry, 15% growth) grew better than acute (60%, 11%) and MNCs (16% share, 17% growth) grew ahead of Indian players (84% share, 13%).
- [Slide without content] The deck carries an 'Upcoming Launches' slide whose contents did not survive text extraction, so the pipeline/launch detail is not available here.

deepdive.thesis: GSK India delivered its first INR1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, driven by supply normalization in GenMeds and strong oncology vaccine launches, with EBITDA margin expanding to 35.9% — the key change is the transition from volume-driven generics to high-margin specialty assets like Zejula/Jemperli and Shingrix, which now define future growth and margin sustainability.

open.item: Directors recommended a final dividend of Rs. 57 per equity share for FY2025-26, subject to Member approval at the AGM on 30th June 2026, absorbing Rs. 966 crores, payable on or after 1st July 2026.
Company will significantly scale up investments in Oncology over the next few years towards its mission of a cancer-free India.
Company is preparing to enter the haemato-oncology space with the launch of Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin) for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma.
Entry of Arexvy, a vaccine to prevent lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV in older adults and high-risk populations, to further strengthen the vaccines portfolio.
26 ongoing and planned global and local clinical trials being conducted in India, including trials for Bepirovirsen aimed at a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B.

Following FY2025-26 supply chain disruptions that materially impacted performance, Company is investing in stronger contingency planning, alternate manufacturing options and improved end-to-end visibility to safeguard business continuity.
Jemperli is progressing through approval for expanded indications across other solid tumours, beyond its first-line approval for primary advanced and recurrent endometrial cancer.
Company recalibrated its Shingrix strategy to focus on patient cohorts with cardiovascular and metabolic disease (CVMD) conditions, recognising their higher shingles risk.
Company accelerated efforts to bridge gaps in maternal and second-year childhood vaccination through integrated engagement and direct parent education.

Company is exploring additional access channels for adult vaccination through collaborations with private hospitals, armed forces and railways, alongside joint business partnerships with strategic hospital partners to expand institutional access.

drhp.business: GSK operates across three business verticals in India — General Medicines, Vaccines and Specialty Medicines — spanning preventive healthcare (vaccines), primary care and advanced curative/specialty therapies. The General Medicines portfolio (Anti-Infectives, Pain Management, Hormones, Dermatology) anchors the business and contributes more than 80% of revenue, while the Company is building out Adult Vaccines, Respiratory Care and, since 2025, Oncology as newer growth engines.

risks.note: Governments, particularly in the US and EU, are prioritising domestic drug manufacturing and supply-chain localisation amid tariff uncertainty and trade tensions, creating policy risk for the globally integrated biopharma supply chains GSK's India operations are part of.
risks.risk: Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty in major markets

risks.note: Despite governments viewing biopharma as a key growth engine, growing pressure on drug pricing continues across major markets, a structural constraint on industry margins.

As a large manufacturer of antibiotics, the Company faces regulatory and reputational risk tied to AMR; its global strategy commits to certifying all internal antibiotic-manufacturing sites by end of 2026, with the Nashik site newly awarded the BSI Kitemark for seven antimicrobial products, subject to annual surveillance audits to retain certification.

The Company is preparing for operationalisation of India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Rules, 2025, requiring strengthened data-privacy/security governance, alongside continued compliance with the Uniform Code of Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP) 2024.
A Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) process is applied during vendor onboarding, indicating reliance on and exposure to external vendors and supply partners.

The Company's Internal Control Framework, Independent Business Monitoring and Management Monitoring exercises are approved/designed by the Global GSK Leadership Team and the Global Risk Oversight and Compliance Council (ROCC), reflecting structural dependence on group-level governance for local risk oversight.
